text:
Nora (Support): customers reporting big p95/p99 tail after we onboarded Atlas-2 yesterday, started around 10:05 PST. Mostly long-sequence jobs (context ~ 64k tokens). errors are timeouts + huge single-token latencies.
Alex (ML Eng): thanks — can you drop an example request payload and a request id?
Nora (Support): one from convo id c-9a3f: context length ~52k tokens, no special functions. header shows model: atlas-2-inference. request id: r_20260305_124501. user reports p99 ~ 18s for next-token. p95 ~ 3.2s. previously atlas-1 p99 ~1.2s for similar.
Priya (Runtime): :eyes: initial guess: kv cache growth or attention kernel fallback for long spans. Any logs from serving?
Jorge (Infra): pulling traces now. I see a cluster of requests routed to gpu-pool-7 and falling back to cpu fallback for some batches — that explains the 18s outliers. Why did fallback trigger?
Alex (ML Eng): Atlas-2 uses a slightly different tokenizer merge table (bpe v3-lite) — tokenization produced ~12% more tokens in some CJK-heavy docs, causing larger sequences and different seq length distribution. Could be pushing runtime to a slow path.
Nora (Support): customer claim: we didn't change client payloads. This only started after the model switch.
Priya (Runtime): can you grep for "kv_cache_resize" and "attention_fallback" in the runtime logs for r_20260305_124501?
Nora (Support): pasted logs from infra:
```
[2026-03-05T17:45:01Z] r_20260305_124501 start route=atlas-2-inference pool=gpu-pool-7
[2026-03-05T17:45:02Z] kv_cache_alloc size=42000000 bytes ok
[2026-03-05T17:45:03Z] attention_kernel check => not_supported_for_seq=65536 fallback=true
[2026-03-05T17:45:19Z] fallback_exec cpu path time=16.8s
[2026-03-05T17:45:20Z] r_20260305_124501 complete status=200
```
Priya (Runtime): that's the smoking gun — atlas-2's layer config hits an attention kernel selector that currently doesn't support that sequence length on the chosen kernel/driver, so it falls back to a slow CPU kernel for the remainder.
Alex (ML Eng): hmm also the tokenizer change increases token count which moves many requests over the threshold where our efficient windowed attention is valid. Two things to consider: revert the bpe table or change kernel selector thresholds.
Jorge (Infra): why did those requests route to gpu-pool-7 which lacks the updated driver set? we rolled a driver upgrade to other pools yesterday but not pool-7. routing policy usually respects region + score. Maybe autoscaler bumped capacity and created new instances with older AMI.
Nora (Support): some users also see intermittent 502s during these tails. Could be memory pressure.
Priya (Runtime): mitigation plan: 1) add a temporary routing rule to steer atlas-2-inference long-context requests to pools with the updated kernels; 2) for immediate relief, put atlas-1 back as a weighted fallback for 30% of traffic; 3) hotfix kernel selector to avoid CPU fallback for known safe ranges.
Alex (ML Eng): to add: a tokenizer compatibility flag in the onboard config that can force use of 'bpe-v2' for now (client-side unchanged, server-side re-tokenize) — low friction rollback for tokenization delta.
Jorge (Infra): I'm pushing a routing override to send requests with context_length > 48000 to gpu-pool-9/10 (they have newer drivers). Command:
```
# temp route override
redwood route update atlas-2-inference --match "context_tokens>48000" --pools gpu-pool-9,gpu-pool-10
```

eng-oncall-bot: deployed route override to 9/10, propagation ~30s.
deploy-bot: canary deploy atlas-2-inference v2.0.1-kernelpatch started on pool-9.
Priya (Runtime): I'll open a hotfix PR to change kernel selector heuristics. quick patch: if token_count > 50k && driver_version < 542 -> prefer alternative gpu kernel instead of cpu fallback.
Alex (ML Eng): also filing a tokenization revert option in model-manifest so we can toggle re-tokenization without redeploying code.
Nora (Support): customers are asking for eta. what do we tell them?
Jorge (Infra): immediate: routing override is live, should push p99 down for affected users within a minute. medium: driver roll across pools ~2–3 hours. long: tokenizer flag + kernel patch same-day rollout if QA-ok.
Priya (Runtime): repro steps (for engs who want to reproduce locally):
```
# reproduce long-tail locally
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '@large_context.json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=atlas-2-inference
# large_context.json should be ~50k tokens when tokenized with bpe-v3-lite
```
Add env var to force old kernel selector: RUNTIME_KV_SELECTOR=legacy to see previous behavior.
Alex (ML Eng): I'll prepare a small test suite of ~100 synthetic sequences (mix of CJK and ascii) to show tokenization delta and kernel path selection.
Nora (Support): customer update drafted: "We're aware of increased tail latency for very long contexts on Atlas-2. We've applied a routing workaround and expect p99 to improve within minutes. Engineering is rolling a kernel selector patch and a tokenizer compatibility toggle; we'll update within the day." :thumbsup:
Jorge (Infra): monitoring dashboards show p99 dropping already in the routed pools.
Priya (Runtime): once kernel-selector PR merges, I'll coordinate a canary patch to apply to pool-7. target ETA 3 hours (QA + canary).
Alex (ML Eng): follow-up note — we should add a model-onboard checklist item: verify tokenization delta vs baseline and run long-seq kernel compatibility tests on all pools before flip.
Nora (Support): thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated and paste customer replies.
Jorge (Infra): marking this thread with incident tag #long-tail-atlas2 for tracking.
Nora (Support): closing loop for now, will reopen if p99 doesn't drop after 15m. :wave:
